title: Experimentation framework for adaptive batching and KV cache A/B tests
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an experiment framework to A/B test adaptive batching and KV cache configurations for production inference traffic. We need a safe way to propose, apply, monitor, and automatically roll back config changes that trade latency for cost. This ticket covers experiment design, instrumentation, dashboard surfaces, automated guardrails, statistical analysis plan, and runbook for applying/rolling back configs in Redwood Dedicated and Hosted routes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary/A/B pipeline exists to assign requests to control and treatment configs for a given route. 2) End-to-end instrumentation captures per-request: routing cohort, latency P50/P95/P99, tokens per request, cost estimate, error rate, model output quality signals, and KV cache hit rate. 3) Dashboards show cohort comparison and automatic alerting on regression thresholds. 4) Automated rollback triggers when safety SLOs degraded beyond thresholds. 5) Experiment analysis notebook and template are available for PM/Eng consumption.
experiment_design: We will run randomized cohort assignment at the route level for 2-week experiments with stratified sampling by request size and customer tier. Cohorts: A (control - current batching & KV cache), B (treatment - adaptive batching profile + aggressive KV cache TTL). Secondary treatments may include per-request batching hints. Allocation: start 5% treatment traffic, ramp to 25% if no safety alerts. Ramp logic performed by orchestration service with human approval at major milestones.
metrics_to_track: Primary: cost per 1k tokens (estimated), tail latency (P95, P99), request success rate. Secondary: KV cache hit rate, average tokens batched per GPU step, model output delta (BLEU/ROUGE-like proxy where applicable), user-visible failure types. Safety metrics: increased error rate, latency SLO breaches, model hallucination proxy (confidence drop), customer-facing 500s.
analysis_plan: Use pre-registered analysis: compute cohort differences with bootstrap confidence intervals for key metrics; correct for multiple comparisons across routes. Calculate cost savings per 1M tokens and estimate annualized impact. Run subgroup analyses by request size bucket and by model family. Define minimum detectable effect (MDE) for cost reduction = 3% with 90% power; sample size calc attached in the experiment notebook link.
dashboards: Create a dedicated dashboard 'Exp: Adaptive Batching + KV Cache' with these panels: cohort selector, live traffic split, cost-per-token over time, latency histograms, KV hit-rate heatmap by hour, alert timeline, and output-quality trend. Panels must support filter by route, model, and customer tier. Add annotations for ramp steps and config changes.
data_collection_and_storage: Log per-request metadata to the experiments telemetry dataset: request_id, timestamp, cohort, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, kv_hit, latency_ms, status_code, cost_estimate, golden_eval_score if available. Retain experiment logs for 90 days in Hot store and archive aggregated results to BigQuery-like warehouse for analysis. Ensure PII not logged; strip request text unless opt-in for evals.
rollout_and_rollback: Rollout policy: 5% -> 10% -> 25% over 72 hours with manual gates. Automated rollback triggers: (a) P95 latency increase > 30% sustained for 15 minutes, (b) error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points absolute, (c) KV cache hit rate drop causing cost > baseline by 10%. When a trigger fires, orchestration will immediately move all treatment traffic back to control and create an incident ticket. Post-rollback: capture heap of logs and run postmortem within 3 business days.
safety_and_validation: Implement dry-run mode that simulates batching behavior and estimates impact without applying to live inference. Add shadow logging to compare what would have been batched/cached. Validate quality using a small set of synthetic golden prompts and sampled customer prompts (opt-in). Require sign-off from SRE and ML quality owners before >10% ramp.
runbook: Steps for engineers: 1) Deploy experiment config to orchestration service in feature flag off state. 2) Run dry-run and verify metrics. 3) Flip to 5% and monitor dashboard for 30 minutes. 4) Follow ramp checklist and handoff sign-offs. 5) If alert fires, follow rollback procedure and notify PM, SRE, and ML owners. Post-experiment: generate experiment report using analysis notebook and present to Cost Optimization weekly sync.
followups: If experiment successful: create task to add recommended configs to Optimize suggestions engine and a plan to A/B test across additional routes. If failed: enumerate hypotheses, schedule targeted micro-experiments (eg. TTL tuning, kernel-level batching tweaks). Update model-specific tuning docs.
notes: Differentiators vs prior experiments: this ticket formalizes automated rollback thresholds and integrates KV cache telemetry into the analysis surface. Aim is to produce a reusable experiment template that Product can reuse for other cost-saving config proposals.
